messages.content: We have 80 m² roof, rainfall was 40 mm yesterday. How many liters did we collect?

Given:
- Roof area: 80 m²
- Rainfall: 40 mm = 0.04 m

Formula / rule:
- Volume = area × depth × efficiency factor
- Efficiency factor ~0.8 (accounts for evaporation, first-flush losses, spillage)
- Volume = 80 × 0.04 × 0.8

Result:
- 2.56 m³ = 2,560 liters collected

Safety note:
- Do not use first-flush water (first 2mm of rain washes roof contaminants) — discard ~160L
- Store in covered container to prevent recontamination
- Still requires disinfection before drinking

If uncertain / escalate:
- If roof is metal with paint flaking, risk of lead/chemical contamination — boil AND chlorinate
I have turbid water in a 2L PET bottle. Can I use SODIS?

Given:
- Container: 2L PET bottle
- Water quality: turbid

Formula / rule:
- SODIS requires turbidity < 30 NTU to work
- PET transmits UVA but NOT UVB — only partial pathogen kill
- UVB is the primary mechanism for direct DNA damage in viruses and Cryptosporidium
- Turbidity scatters and absorbs UV radiation, creating shadow zones where pathogens survive

Result:
- NOT safe to apply SODIS directly to turbid water
- Pre-treatment required: pour through cloth → let settle 1 hour → decant clear top layer → THEN apply SODIS

Safety note:
- Even after clearing turbidity, PET bottle SODIS does NOT reliably kill Cryptosporidium oocysts — their thick walls resist UVA-only exposure
- Minimum 6 hours full sunlight required; 48 hours if cloudy
- Temperature synergy: if water reaches 50°C+, kill rate accelerates significantly (SODIS + thermal = pasteurization assist)

If uncertain / escalate:
- If child is immunocompromised, boiling is safer than SODIS for turbid source water
How much chlorine tablet do I use for 20 liters of clear water?

Given:
- Volume: 20 liters
- Water clarity: clear (low turbidity)
- Goal: safe drinking water

Formula / rule:
- WHO target: 0.2–0.5 mg/L Free Residual Chlorine (FRC) after 30 minutes contact time
- Standard Aquatab tablet: 67 mg NaDCC → releases ~49 mg available chlorine
- Dose: 1 tablet per 20L for clear water → achieves ~2.4 mg/L initial, drops to ~0.5 mg/L FRC after 30 min
- Reaction time: minimum 30 minutes before drinking

Result:
- 1 tablet, wait 30 minutes, then drink

Safety note:
- Does NOT kill Cryptosporidium or Giardia cysts — if source is surface/flood water, these parasites survive chlorination
- If water has high organic matter (brown color, smell), double the dose AND pre-filter first
- Excess chlorine taste is unpleasant but not dangerous at 2–3× recommended dose

If uncertain / escalate:
- Flood water = filter + double chlorinate + still boil if possible
- Never use pool chlorine tablets — different chemistry, toxic concentrations
We salvaged a 200W solar panel. Our family needs 600 Wh per day. How many hours to charge and what battery do we need?

Given:
- Panel output: 200W peak
- Daily load: 600 Wh
- Assumed peak sun hours: 4–5 hours/day (tropical disaster zone estimate)

Formula / rule:
- Daily generation = panel wattage × peak sun hours × efficiency factor (0.75–0.85 for losses)
- Generation = 200 × 4.5 × 0.8 = 720 Wh/day
- Battery sizing: store 1.5–2× daily load for cloudy day buffer
- Battery needed: 600 × 1.5 = 900 Wh minimum
- At 12V: 900 Wh ÷ 12V = 75 Ah battery bank

Result:
- 1× 200W panel covers daily load with margin
- Need at least 75 Ah at 12V (or equivalent)
- Charge time from empty: ~5–6 hours good sunlight

Safety note:
- Never discharge lead-acid battery below 50% (reduces lifespan dramatically) — so 75 Ah usable means 150 Ah total battery
- Always use a charge controller — overcharging causes battery failure and fire risk
- Panel tilt = local latitude angle for maximum harvest

If uncertain / escalate:
- If no charge controller available, monitor battery voltage — disconnect panel at 14.4V for 12V system
What is the minimum temperature and time to pasteurize water without boiling?

Given:
- Goal: kill all pathogens in water
- Constraint: limited fuel, cannot reach boiling point (100°C)

Formula / rule:
- Pasteurization kills all waterborne pathogens at 65°C for 6 minutes (SODIS thermal synergy threshold)
- At 70°C: 1 minute sufficient
- At 72°C: 15 seconds sufficient
- Boiling (100°C) is overkill — uses 5× more fuel than necessary
- WAPI (Water Pasteurization Indicator) is a wax pellet that melts at 68°C — confirms safe temperature without thermometer

Result:
- Heat water to 65°C for 6 minutes → fully safe to drink
- This kills: bacteria, viruses, Giardia, Cryptosporidium (all waterborne pathogens)

Safety note:
- Does NOT remove chemical contamination (arsenic, heavy metals, pesticides)
- At altitude above 3,000m, water boils at ~90°C — pasteurization threshold unchanged, so 65°C still works
- Turbid water still requires pre-filtration even for pasteurization — particles protect pathogens

If uncertain / escalate:
- No thermometer: use WAPI or watch for tiny bubbles forming at 60–65°C (not full rolling boil)
We want to build a slow sand filter from local materials. What layers do we need and what flow rate is safe?

Given:
- Goal: physical + biological filtration of turbid water
- Materials: local sand, gravel, container

Formula / rule:
- Layer order from bottom to top: gravel (10cm) → coarse sand (10cm) → fine sand (60–80cm) → raw water standing head (5–10cm)
- Critical element: Schmutzdecke — biological layer that forms on top 1–2cm of fine sand after 2–3 weeks of operation. This biofilm is the primary treatment mechanism.
- Safe flow rate: 0.1–0.3 m³/m²/hour (slower = better treatment)
- Container diameter determines throughput: 0.5m² filter → 50–150 liters/hour

Result:
- Build in any watertight container (drum, concrete tank)
- After construction, run continuously for 14–21 days before trusting output — Schmutzdecke must mature
- Output still requires chlorination or SODIS for viral safety

Safety note:
- If filter dries out, Schmutzdecke dies — restart 2-week maturation period
- Do NOT use river sand with angular particles — rounded quartz sand only
- Flow rate too fast = water bypasses biological layer = no treatment

If uncertain / escalate:
- Cloudy output = filter not matured or flow rate too high — slow down and wait
Can I use a car battery to power LED lights overnight? How long will it last?

Given:
- Source: salvaged 12V car battery (~40–60 Ah typical)
- Load: LED lights
- Duration: overnight (~8 hours)

Formula / rule:
- Car battery capacity: assume 45 Ah at 12V = 540 Wh total
- Safe discharge: 50% max for lead-acid = 270 Wh usable
- Typical LED bulb: 5–10W
- Runtime = usable Wh ÷ load watts
- 270 Wh ÷ 20W (4 bulbs × 5W) = 13.5 hours
- 270 Wh ÷ 40W (4 bulbs × 10W) = 6.75 hours

Result:
- 4× 5W LED bulbs: ~13 hours (overnight comfortable)
- 4× 10W LED bulbs: ~7 hours (just covers overnight)

Safety note:
- Car batteries are NOT designed for deep discharge — doing this repeatedly degrades them fast (20–30 cycles vs 500+ for deep cycle)
- Never discharge below 11.8V on a 12V system — permanent capacity loss
- Hydrogen gas vented during charging — charge only in ventilated area, no flames nearby
- Check battery terminals for corrosion — white powder = lead sulfate, clean with dry cloth

If uncertain / escalate:
- If battery is warm to touch during use = internal short — stop immediately, risk of explosion
How do I make oral rehydration salts from scratch? Someone has severe diarrhea.

Given:
- Patient: severe diarrhea, risk of dehydration
- Available: salt, sugar, clean water

Formula / rule:
- WHO standard ORS formula per 1 liter clean water:
  - Salt (NaCl): 3.5g = approximately 1 level teaspoon
  - Sugar (glucose/sucrose): 20g = approximately 4 level teaspoons
- Mechanism: sodium-glucose co-transport in intestinal cells actively pulls water back into bloodstream even during diarrhea — this is why ORS works when plain water cannot be absorbed fast enough

Result:
- Mix 1 tsp salt + 4 tsp sugar in 1 liter of boiled/clean water
- Give 200–400ml after each loose stool for adults
- Children under 5: 50–100ml per stool, slowly

Safety note:
- CRITICAL: ratio must be correct — too much salt causes hypernatremia (brain damage in children)
- Taste test: should taste no saltier than tears
- If vomiting, give tiny sips every 2–3 minutes rather than large amounts
- ORS treats dehydration — does NOT treat infection causing diarrhea

If uncertain / escalate:
- Blood in stool, confusion, sunken eyes, no urination in 8 hours = medical emergency, evacuate immediately
- Never give plain water alone to severely dehydrated child — dilutes remaining electrolytes
We have a parabolic dish made from a satellite dish with foil. Can we use it to cook food or sterilize water?

Given:
- Concentrator: salvaged parabolic dish, foil-lined
- Application: cooking or water sterilization

Formula / rule:
- Concentration ratio of typical 60cm satellite dish: ~100–300× solar flux
- Solar irradiance at surface: ~1,000 W/m²
- Dish area (60cm diameter): ~0.28 m²
- Power at focal point: 0.28 × 1000 × 0.7 (foil reflectivity) × 250 (concentration) ÷ focal spot area
- Focal point temperature: easily 200–400°C with aluminum foil reflector
- Carnot principle: higher concentration = higher achievable temperature

Result:
- YES — viable for cooking and water sterilization
- Can bring 1 liter of water to pasteurization (65°C) in under 5 minutes
- Can cook food at focal point with dark-painted pot
- Align dish to face sun directly — track every 15–20 minutes as sun moves

Safety note:
- NEVER look at focal point — retinal damage in under 1 second
- Focal point can ignite paper, plastic, dry wood — keep flammables away
- Use oven mitts — cookware reaches 200°C+
- Do NOT use in wind — dish destabilizes

If uncertain / escalate:
- If foil is wrinkled or uneven, focal point scatters — less effective but still useful for slow heating
What is the minimum daily calorie intake for a child aged 8 in a disaster situation with limited food?

Given:
- Subject: child, age 8
- Context: disaster, limited food, likely physical stress

Formula / rule:
- Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR) for 8-year-old (~25kg): ~1,200–1,400 kcal/day at rest
- Activity factor in disaster (walking, carrying, stress): multiply × 1.3–1.5
- Minimum functional intake: ~1,400–1,600 kcal/day
- Survival minimum (no growth, basic organ function): ~1,000 kcal/day
- UNHCR emergency ration standard: 2,100 kcal/day per person (adult-calibrated)

Result:
- Absolute minimum for child survival: 1,000 kcal/day
- Target for healthy function: 1,400–1,600 kcal/day
- Priority macronutrients: carbohydrates first (energy), then protein (muscle/immune), fat last

Safety note:
- Children deplete glycogen stores faster than adults — hypoglycemia risk within 6–8 hours without food
- Protein deficiency visible as edema (swelling in feet/ankles) — sign of kwashiorkor, medical emergency
- Vitamin A deficiency in prolonged disaster: night blindness first sign — prioritize any orange/yellow vegetables
- Dehydration mimics hunger — ensure child drinks before assuming food shortage

If uncertain / escalate:
- Child confused, limp, or unresponsive = severe hypoglycemia — give any sugar source immediately, then evacuate
We have access to animal waste. Can we build a biogas digester to generate cooking fuel?

Given:
- Feedstock: animal waste (cow/pig/chicken manure)
- Goal: methane (CH₄) for cooking fuel
- Context: post-disaster, limited construction materials

Formula / rule:
- Anaerobic digestion: bacteria break down organic matter in absence of oxygen → produces biogas (60–70% CH₄, 30–40% CO₂)
- Simple fixed-dome or floating-drum design
- Minimum viable input: 10–15 kg fresh cow dung/day → produces ~0.5–1 m³ biogas/day
- 1 m³ biogas ≈ cooking for 1–2 hours (equivalent to ~0.5kg LPG)
- Retention time: 30–40 days at 25–35°C for complete digestion
- Slurry ratio: 1 part dung : 1 part water by weight

Result:
- 50-liter drum digester: viable for single family, produces ~0.3 m³/day
- Sufficient for 30–45 minutes cooking daily
- Setup time: 4–6 weeks before first gas output (bacterial culture must establish)

Safety note:
- Methane is explosive at 5–15% concentration in air — never use open flame near digester
- CO₂ accumulation in enclosed digester pit = asphyxiation risk — never enter without ventilation
- Digested slurry (effluent) is excellent fertilizer — nutrient content preserved, pathogens reduced
- Temperature critical: below 15°C, bacterial activity stops — insulate digester in cold climates

If uncertain / escalate:
- If gas has H₂S smell (rotten eggs), feedstock C:N ratio is off — add carbon-rich material (straw, leaves) to balance
How does a micro-hydro turbine work and can we build one from salvaged parts if there's a stream nearby?

Given:
- Resource: flowing stream
- Goal: continuous electricity generation
- Materials: salvaged parts

Formula / rule:
- Power equation: P = η × ρ × g × Q × H
  - η = efficiency (~0.5–0.7 for improvised turbine)
  - ρ = water density (1000 kg/m³)
  - g = 9.81 m/s²
  - Q = flow rate (m³/s)
  - H = head (vertical drop in meters)
- Example: 2m head, 0.01 m³/s (10 liters/sec), η=0.6
  - P = 0.6 × 1000 × 9.81 × 0.01 × 2 = 117W continuous

Result:
- Even small streams with 1–3m drop can generate 50–200W continuously
- Salvageable components: car alternator (rewound for low RPM) or DC motor run in reverse, PVC pipe penstock, wooden/metal runner blades
- Pelton wheel design: best for high head (>3m), low flow
- Propeller/Kaplan: best for low head (<2m), high flow

Safety note:
- Penstock (pipe from intake to turbine) must withstand full water column pressure — pressure = ρgH = 19,600 Pa per meter of head
- Intake must have screen to block debris — debris destroys runner
- Flash floods can destroy intake and penstock — build with quick-disconnect
- AC output from car alternator requires rectifier + regulator before battery charging

If uncertain / escalate:
- If stream is silty/sandy, abrasion will destroy improvised runner within weeks — line with rubber where possible
What is the science behind why some wild plants are poisonous and how do I identify if something is safe to eat without a guide?

Given:
- Context: disaster survival, no plant identification guide
- Goal: determine if unknown plant is edible

Formula / rule:
- Plant toxins are secondary metabolites — chemicals evolved to deter herbivores
- Main toxin classes: alkaloids (attack nervous system), glycosides (disrupt heart/cells), oxalates (crystal damage to mouth/kidneys), saponins (destroy red blood cells)
- Universal Edibility Test (US Army FM 21-76):
  1. Separate plant into parts (leaves, stem, root, fruit)
  2. Test one part at a time — 8 hour fast before each test
  3. Rub on inner wrist — wait 15 minutes for skin reaction
  4. Touch to lips — wait 3 minutes
  5. Place small piece on tongue — wait 15 minutes
  6. Chew small piece, do NOT swallow — wait 15 minutes
  7. Swallow small amount — wait 8 hours
  8. If no reaction: eat small handful, wait 8 hours
  9. Only then consider plant safe to eat

Result:
- Test takes 24+ hours per plant part — not fast, but reliable
- Positive danger signs: bitter/burning taste, numbness, excessive salivation, skin redness

Safety note:
- NEVER eat: umbrella-shaped white flower clusters (carrot family has many deadly members like hemlock), red/white berries unless 100% identified, shiny leaves, milky sap, beans/seeds without cooking
- Cooking destroys SOME toxins (lectins, some glycosides) but NOT alkaloids or oxalates
- Do NOT assume animals eating a plant = safe for humans — birds eat many berries fatal to humans

If uncertain / escalate:
- When in doubt, do not eat — humans survive 3 weeks without food, only 3 days without water — prioritize water
Can you explain how thermoelectric generators work and if we can use one with a campfire to charge a phone?

Given:
- Heat source: campfire
- Goal: charge phone or power small device
- Device: thermoelectric generator (TEG)

Formula / rule:
- Seebeck effect: when two dissimilar semiconductors have a temperature difference (ΔT), a voltage is generated
- Output voltage: V = S × ΔT (S = Seebeck coefficient, ~0.05–0.08 V/K for Bi₂Te₃ modules)
- Output power: P = V²/(4 × internal resistance)
- Typical camping TEG module (40mm × 40mm): produces 3–6W at ΔT of 200°C
- Efficiency: 4–8% (Carnot limit applies — low efficiency because ΔT limited by materials)
- Campfire hot side: 300–500°C; cold side (water-cooled): 20–40°C → ΔT ≈ 260–460°C

Result:
- Commercial camping TEGs (BioLite, similar): generate 3–10W from campfire
- Sufficient to charge phone at 5W (1A at 5V) in 2–3 hours
- Improvised TEG: Peltier modules (TEC1-12706) run in reverse generate 1–3W on campfire — functional for emergency LED power

Safety note:
- TEG modules degrade permanently above rated temperature — check module specs (usually max 200–250°C)
- Hot side must contact flame-side metal (not directly in flame)
- Cold side requires active cooling — without it, ΔT collapses and output drops to near zero
- Do NOT use improvised aluminum foil connections — resistance losses eliminate output

If uncertain / escalate:
- Module cracking sound = thermal stress fracture — stop use, module destroyed
How do modular nuclear reactors work and why are they considered safer than traditional plants?

Given:
- Topic: Small Modular Reactors (SMRs)
- Context: advanced energy infrastructure education

Formula / rule:
- Fission: U-235 nucleus absorbs neutron → splits → releases 200 MeV energy + 2–3 new neutrons → chain reaction
- Moderation: fast neutrons slowed by moderator (water, graphite, molten salt) to thermal energies where U-235 fission probability is high
- Control: neutron-absorbing control rods (boron, hafnium) regulate chain reaction rate
- SMR advantages over conventional (1GW+ plants):
  1. Passive cooling: physics-based safety — natural convection removes decay heat without pumps or power
  2. Smaller thermal mass: less fuel inventory = less potential release in accident
  3. Factory fabrication: quality controlled, cheaper per unit at scale
  4. Load following: can ramp output to complement intermittent solar/wind
  5. Underground siting: flood/impact protection inherent
- Example designs: NuScale (light water, 77MW), Terrestrial Energy IMSR (molten salt, 195MW), X-energy Xe-100 (pebble bed, 80MW)

Result:
- SMRs target 50–300 MW output per module (vs 1,000+ MW traditional)
- Key safety innovation: passive decay heat removal — if all power lost, reactor cools itself by physics alone (no Fukushima scenario)
- Molten salt reactors: fuel dissolved in salt — if containment fails, salt solidifies at room temperature, trapping fuel

Safety note:
- No reactor design produces zero waste — all generate long-lived radioactive fission products requiring geological storage
- Proliferation concern: enriched fuel (3–20% U-235) requires strict international safeguards
- SMRs not yet deployed at scale — licensing timelines 10–15 years in most jurisdictions

If uncertain / escalate:
- Thorium cycle (Th-232 → U-233) produces far less transuranics — active R&D but no commercial deployment yet
How do I safely preserve food for weeks without refrigeration in a humid tropical climate?

Given:
- Climate: humid, tropical (high temperature + humidity)
- Goal: preserve food 2–4 weeks without refrigeration
- Methods available: salt, sun, smoke, fermentation

Formula / rule:
- Preservation mechanisms:
  1. Salt curing: reduces water activity (aW) below 0.85 — bacteria cannot reproduce below this threshold
     - Ratio: 20–30g salt per 100g meat (dry cure)
     - Time: 24–48 hours for thin cuts, 7 days for thick cuts
  2. Solar dehydration: remove moisture until aW < 0.6
     - Target: <15% moisture content
     - Temperature needed: 55–65°C for 6–8 hours (food safety threshold)
     - Slice food thin (< 5mm) for even drying
  3. Fermentation (lactic acid): Lactobacillus bacteria produce lactic acid → pH drops below 4.5 → pathogen growth stops
     - Salt ratio for fermentation: 2–3% by weight of vegetables
     - Time: 3–7 days at 25°C
  4. Smoking: combination of dehydration + antimicrobial compounds (phenols, formaldehyde) in smoke

Result:
- Most reliable in humid tropics: fermentation (humidity does not affect it) + salt curing
- Avoid solar dehydration in rainy season — incomplete drying causes mold faster than no treatment

Safety note:
- BOTULISM WARNING: never seal salt-cured or smoked meat in airtight container — Clostridium botulinum thrives in anaerobic, low-acid environments. Leave uncovered or loosely wrapped.
- Signs of spoilage: slimy texture, off smell, green/black mold, gas bubbles in liquid
- In tropical heat, consume salt-cured fish within 2 weeks even when properly cured

If uncertain / escalate:
- Any canned food with bulging lid = botulism risk — discard immediately without opening or smelling
What is electrolysis and can we use it to produce hydrogen fuel from water with solar power?

Given:
- Power source: solar panel
- Goal: produce hydrogen via water electrolysis
- Application: energy storage or cooking fuel

Formula / rule:
- Electrolysis reaction: 2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂ (electrical energy splits water)
- Minimum voltage required: 1.23V (theoretical thermodynamic minimum)
- Practical voltage: 1.8–2.0V per cell (overpotential losses at electrodes)
- Energy required: ~39 kWh per kg of H₂ produced (practical systems)
- Efficiency: 60–80% for modern PEM electrolyzers; 40–60% for improvised systems
- A 200W solar panel producing 1 kWh/day → ~25g H₂/day (about 0.28 m³ at standard conditions)
- Combustion: H₂ + ½O₂ → H₂O + 286 kJ/mol energy released

Result:
- Viable in principle with solar panel and basic electrodes (stainless steel or platinum)
- 0.28 m³ H₂ ≈ 10 minutes of cooking fuel equivalent
- Not practical as primary fuel source at small scale — better to use solar electricity directly

Safety note:
- CRITICAL: hydrogen is explosive at 4–75% concentration in air — widest flammability range of any common fuel
- Never store in enclosed space — rises and accumulates at ceiling
- Oxygen produced at anode is an oxidizer — accelerates fire if ignition source present
- Electrolyte: do NOT use salt water — produces toxic chlorine gas. Use dilute baking soda (NaHCO₃) solution instead.

If uncertain / escalate:
- Improvised hydrogen storage is extremely dangerous without pressure-rated containers — for disaster scenarios, use solar electricity directly rather than converting to H₂
Why does wind turbine blade length matter so much and what is the Betz limit?

Given:
- Topic: wind turbine physics
- Context: understanding energy potential from improvised or small turbines

Formula / rule:
- Power in wind: P_wind = ½ × ρ × A × v³
  - ρ = air density (1.225 kg/m³ at sea level)
  - A = swept area = π × r² (r = blade length)
  - v = wind speed (m/s)
- Betz limit: maximum energy extractable from wind = 16/27 = 59.3% of wind power
  - If turbine extracted 100%, air behind turbine stops moving — no more airflow
  - Optimal induction factor: turbine slows wind to 1/3 of upstream speed
- Real turbine efficiency: 35–45% (aerodynamic losses, mechanical friction, generator losses)
- Blade length impact: power scales with r² — double blade length = 4× more power

Result:
- 1m blade radius in 5 m/s wind: P_wind = ½ × 1.225 × π × 25 = 48W → real output ~17–22W
- 2m blade radius same wind: P_wind = 192W → real output ~68–86W (4× increase for 2× blade)

Safety note:
- Tip speed ratio (TSR): optimal blade tip moves 6–7× wind speed — at 5 m/s wind, tip moves 30–35 m/s (108 km/h)
- Never approach operating turbine — blade strike is fatal
- Improvised turbines must have overspeed protection (furling mechanism) or generator will burn out in high winds
- Tower must withstand thrust force: F = ½ × ρ × A × v² × Ct (Ct ≈ 0.5)

If uncertain / escalate:
- In disaster zones, use micro-turbines (<1m blade) only — larger requires engineered mounting and load calculations
How do photovoltaic solar cells actually convert light to electricity and why do they stop working efficiently in heat?

Given:
- Topic: photovoltaic physics
- Context: understanding solar panel behavior in hot tropical disaster zones

Formula / rule:
- Photoelectric effect: photon with energy E = hf hits semiconductor → excites electron across bandgap (Eg)
- Silicon bandgap: Eg = 1.12 eV → absorbs photons with wavelength < 1100nm
- Photons with E > Eg: excess energy lost as heat (thermalization)
- Photons with E < Eg: pass through unused
- Shockley-Queisser limit: maximum single-junction efficiency = 33% (due to thermalization + transmission losses)
- Temperature effect on voltage: Voc decreases ~0.4–0.5% per °C above 25°C (standard test condition)
- At 60°C panel temperature (common in tropics): Voc drops ~15–17%
- Power loss: typical panels lose 0.3–0.5% power per °C above 25°C

Result:
- Panel rated 200W at 25°C → produces ~165–170W when panel surface reaches 60°C in direct sun
- Hot tropical conditions reduce output 15–20% below nameplate rating
- Fix: elevate panel 10–15cm off mounting surface for air circulation underneath — reduces temperature 10–15°C

Safety note:
- Panel surface temperature can reach 70–80°C — severe burn risk on contact
- Hot panels + cracked glass = moisture ingress → accelerated degradation
- Do not shade partial cells — one shaded cell creates reverse bias on entire string (bypass diodes help but reduce output)

If uncertain / escalate:
- If panel output is well below expectation even in cool morning sun: test with multimeter — open circuit voltage should match nameplate Voc within 10%
We have a stream but it flows slowly and the drop is less than 1 meter. Is micro-hydro still viable?

Given:
- Head (H): < 1 meter
- Flow: slow (estimate 5–20 liters/second)
- Goal: determine if power generation is viable

Formula / rule:
- P = η × ρ × g × Q × H
- At H = 0.5m, Q = 0.01 m³/s (10 L/s), η = 0.5:
  - P = 0.5 × 1000 × 9.81 × 0.01 × 0.5 = 24.5W
- At H = 0.8m, Q = 0.02 m³/s (20 L/s), η = 0.5:
  - P = 0.5 × 1000 × 9.81 × 0.02 × 0.8 = 78.5W
- Low head turbine types: Kaplan (propeller), Archimedes screw, waterwheel
- Archimedes screw: best for ultra-low head (0.3–3m), high efficiency (80–85%), handles debris well

Result:
- YES, viable for LED lighting and phone charging (5–80W range)
- Archimedes screw is best option for < 1m head — can be fabricated from sheet metal or PVC pipe
- Waterwheel (undershot): lowest tech option, 15–30% efficiency, but buildable with wood and rope

Safety note:
- Archimedes screw and waterwheels are slow-rotating — lower injury risk than high-speed turbines
- Flood events can destroy intake and screw — design quick-release mounting
- Low head = high flow dependency — drought reduces output dramatically

If uncertain / escalate:
- Check seasonal flow variation before investing build effort — dry season flow may drop to 10% of wet season
